title: Context Engineering Is a Data Problem — David Gasquez essay
summary: Essay arguing organizational context should be built like a data warehouse: extract raw sources, transform into org-specific models, and publish curated text artifacts for agents. Treats knowledge bases as compilers and curated files as materialized views optimized for LLM consumption.
question_it_answers: Why should agent context be modeled like a data warehouse instead of stuffing every raw source into prompts?

claims.text: Context engineering is extract-filter-curate-model-publish work, analogous to analytics ETL.
claims.evidence: Context engineering is that same work: extracting, filtering, curating, modeling, and publishing artifacts to help the organization make better decisions.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: A knowledge base should compile raw sources into LLM-optimized representations via extract, transform, publish stages.
claims.evidence: Knowledge base as **compiler for agents** — raw sources → LLM-optimized representations.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: Teams need per-area marts rather than one universal company context package.
claims.evidence: Build **marts** per area/team — no universal "company context" package
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: Gasquez’s public handbook vault (davidgasquez/handbook) is 159 topic .md files in a flat wiki-link tree, including Context Engineering.md and Company Knowledge Management.md. It is a personal published vault, not a company Slack extract.
claims.evidence: Git trees/main: 164 blobs / 159 md. Context Engineering.md 5989 B restates extract/transform/publish and no single company brain.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge
